'deep learning frameworks' is a taxonomy alias of deep-learning. It is the broad skill named alongside its examples, so it stays out of the group.
PyTorch and Tensor Flow are offered as e.g. examples for one ask, so they form alternative_group 1.
'Tensor Flow' is quoted verbatim as written in the posting (spaced spelling).
The deep learning mention under the stand-out section collapses into the required deep-learning criterion.
LiDAR/camera perception and multi-sensor fusion have no taxonomy entry. I did not map them to computer-vision, because the posting never names computer vision; they are listed as unmapped.
'debugging skills' is not mapped to testing, because the testing alias is 'debugging & testing' and debugging alone is not that.
'Building and sustaining training and essential metric workflows for large-scale datasets' is not mapped to model-development or data-pipelines. Neither is clearly named, which is the literal reading.
'mathematical foundations of ML' is covered by machine-learning.
The 'data pipelines' mention is left unlabeled because it appears only in responsibilities.
TensorRT is a single e.g. example, so it gets no group.
I included inference-optimization from 'model optimization for real-time inference' but flagged it uncertain.
Degree takes the highest level named: 'MS or PhD' gives phd. 'or equivalent experience' sets degree_or_equivalent to true.
Seniority is stated from the 'Senior' title. The '8+ years' phrase agrees with it.
